title: India's IT giants are in trouble (weak guidance cycle)
thesis: TCS-anchored weak-print analogs (8 events, 2021-2025) show a consistent defensive rotation: FMCG/staples outperform IT on and after weak guidance quarters (defensive CAAR +0.60%, t=2.00, p=0.046 — the only statistically clean signal in the study). IT names' own CAARs are insignificant (|t|<1). Strategy C (defensive basket) is the primary expression; B (FMCG vs IT-SSF pair) is the market-neutral alternative. All backtests verdict UNPROVEN (8 events; MinTRL 56–937 obs gap is the binding constraint).
time_horizon: 4–8 weeks per event (held around weak guidance quarter print)

title: Monsoon trade — Kharif season rural positioning (India)
thesis: India's Kharif crop cycle creates a repeatable seasonal edge: (1) Forecast run-up: tractor (M&M) and 2W (TVSMOTOR) outperform in Apr15-Jun15 regardless of market direction, once beta-stripped vs NIFTY future (CAAR +7.46%, t=2.83, p=0.005; trust verdict PROMISING, conf=97). (2) Sowing window: agri-input basket (COROMANDEL/RALLIS/UPL) outperforms only in IMD-confirmed-normal monsoon years (9/16 yr win-rate 78%). (3) M&M directional call spread (defined-risk) captures monsoon-beta upside. S2 is the core; S1 is the IMD-confirmation satellite; S3 the optional overlay.
time_horizon: Seasonal (Apr–Sep annually; S2 core Apr15–Jun15, S1 Jun-Aug, S3 Apr-Sep)

title: Crude / Geopolitical shock: de-escalation importer trade (crude-DOWN only)
thesis: 2010-2026 backtest (4,272 rows, 67-71 triggered episodes): the de-escalation / crude-DOWN leg (Brent 10d ≤ -8%) has a positive, cost-surviving Expression dial B/78 (CAAR alignment 80%, p=0.012, cost-survival 67%). The importer basket (ASIANPAINT/BERGEPAINT/INDIGO/HINDPETRO/BPCL/IOC) is the only placeable expression. Critical out-of-sample finding: the escalation/crude-UP leg (Strategies B and C) does NOT hold up — B is NO_EDGE (−42%, 78% bootstrap paths lose, loss_likely flag) and C is NO_EDGE convex insurance with near-zero standalone edge. ONLY deploy Strategy A (crude-DOWN / de-escalation satellite).
time_horizon: ~20-day episode hold per Brent-signal trigger (de-escalation / crude-DOWN only)

title: RBI cuts the repo rate at the next MPC meeting
thesis: A rate-cut cycle lowers funding costs and supports credit growth and EMI-sensitive demand; banks and NBFCs are the primary beneficiaries, life insurers a relative loser.

title: Will digital-payments / fintech beat the market this year?
thesis: India's digital-payment boom (UPI) may lift finance-tech companies above the market.

title: Will nuclear energy make a major comeback before 2027?
thesis: India's power-building boom lifts big power and engineering firms (nuclear pure-plays aren't listed here).

title: Will Nifty touch 30,000 before year-end?
thesis: The whole Indian market would need to climb about a quarter more to reach 30,000.

title: Will Middle-East tensions escalate further this quarter?
thesis: When conflict flares, oil and gold tend to rise, helping oil producers and defence firms.

title: Will AI replace traditional search engines?
thesis: Newer, faster-moving Indian tech firms may do better than the giant established ones as AI reshapes the industry.

title: Will EV sales increase more than expected this year?
thesis: If electric-vehicle sales grow faster than expected, the whole EV supply chain benefits.

title: Will AI create more jobs than it destroys by 2027?
thesis: As AI spreads, India's big IT & software companies get more work — and their shares tend to rise.

title: Will a major geopolitical conflict flare up?
thesis: Defence primes are the consistent reactor when conflict erupts — Raytheon, Lockheed, General Dynamics and Northrop rise on order-flow expectations.

title: Will a major hurricane make US landfall?
thesis: Insurers — not homebuilders — are the real post-hurricane winners: damage comes in less bad than feared and pricing power rises. Homebuilders actually fell.

title: Will a major foreign app get banned?
thesis: Every time a TikTok-style ban loomed, Snap picked up the displaced users and ad dollars — the proven beneficiary of the ban mechanism.

title: Will Bitcoin make a fresh all-time high?
thesis: When Bitcoin prints a new all-time high, risk-on flows rotate into the #2 coin — Ethereum has historically outrun BTC itself in the month after.

title: Will Gold prices rise?
thesis: Hold the metal itself, through ETFs, rather than the companies that trade in it.

title: Will MicroStrategy announce another big Bitcoin buy?
thesis: Saylor's BTC-treasury buys reliably lift the listed Bitcoin proxies; MSTR itself is the cleanest one-month reactor.

title: Will Elon Musk post bullishly about crypto again?
thesis: Across six real Musk pro-Dogecoin posts, the durable one-month winners were the Bitcoin miners and Solana — leveraged proxies that outran DOGE itself.

title: Will a court rule against Big Tech?
thesis: Counter-intuitively, Google rallied after 'guilty' antitrust rulings — because the market had priced a forced break-up, and every ruling that stopped short was a relief.

title: Will a Chinese lab ship a surprise AI model?
thesis: A Chinese AI breakthrough re-rates the Chinese tech leaders — Alibaba, the listed China-AI proxy, jumped after DeepSeek.

title: Will a major crypto exchange be hit by regulators?
thesis: When a rival exchange is taken down, the surviving listed exchange inherits the flow — Coinbase jumped when Binance's CZ pleaded guilty.

title: Will Adani win a new project abroad?
thesis: Adani's overseas port/energy wins accrue straight to the group itself — Adani Ports is the direct, clean expression of the belief.

title: Will a major bank need a rescue?
thesis: The acquirer/survivor of a forced bank rescue takes share on favourable terms — UBS rose after absorbing Credit Suisse.

title: Will India have a good monsoon this season?
thesis: A strong monsoon lifts rural demand — tractors, fertilisers, two-wheelers and FMCG.

title: Will renewable energy grow over the years?
thesis: India's solar, wind and grid build-out lifts the power producers and equipment makers behind it.
